messages:
Emma Li: Thinking about combining locality-aware prefetch with deferred eviction. If we prefetch into local KV for predicted next prefixes, how should eviction bailouts reconcile with the lease system? can we avoid a lot of lease churn?
Jun Park: tl;dr: prefer soft leases for prefetch entries and add a reconciliation window. strict ownership will churn leases.
Ryan Chen: agree. soft lease = mark candidates for compaction rather than immediate eviction. reduces churn but may use memory.
Maya Shah: this helps microbursts. question: how do we expose this via admission? callers pass deadline hints or we infer from token budget?
Emma Li: sketch: admit(request) -> {slot_id, lease_id, prefetch_hint}. prefetch_hint has locality_score 0..100. runtime prefetches when score>70. if headroom < watermark then mark prefetch entries bailout=true.
Jun Park: add async reconcile loop: if lease mismatch > N ms owner can escalate to hard eviction to avoid dangling prefetched KV.
Ryan Chen: tradeoff: hard eviction frees mem but can spike latency on repeats. soft + TTL seems sane.
Maya Shah: telemetry needed: prefetch_hits, prefetch_evictions_bailout, reconcile_time_ms, lease_escalations. add to batcher metrics.
Emma Li: also want a "prefetch harms fairness" signal (tenant A prefetching evicts B).
Jun Park: weight prefetch_score by tenant_budget_factor so big tenants don't hog.
Ryan Chen: implementation: keep prefetched entries in a per-lane soft pool, not a global pool; global only in critical headroom events.
Maya Shah: lanes reduce GC thrash but can starve each other. add a global backpressure signal when GPU mem > watermark.
Emma Li: proposal: three watermarks: safe, soft, critical. on soft mark prefetch bailouts; on critical escalate leases and block new prefetches.
Ryan Chen: suggested defaults: safe=60% mem, soft=80%, critical=92% (configurable per-machine).
Maya Shah: reconcile windows? fast 200ms for same-host, slow 2s for remote. cancel remote prefetch if headroom hits soft.
Ryan Chen: record prefetch_aborts with reason tag (bailout|reconcile_timeout|evicted).
Jun Park: add test harness: synthetic hotspot replay + tenant skew; measure p99, eviction rates, fairness delta.
Maya Shah: I'll add runtime-ci test: two tenants, one hotspotting, one cold; run 10k requests and measure fairness.
Emma Li: admission API sketch:
```
admit(request) -> {slot_id, lease_id, prefetch_hint: {score:int, expected_next_tokens:int}}
```
reconcile_lease(lease_id) -> {status: "ok" | "escalated" | "stale"}  (accept optional owner_hint).
Ryan Chen: rollout: prefetch=false by default, opt-in per pool. canary -> prefetch=soft, collect 24h metrics, then enable hard if stable.
infra-bot: Deploy note: canary cluster c-3 will accept runtime.prefetch=soft starting 1745010000. watch runtime.prefetch_hits and runtime.lease_escalations.
Maya Shah: add automatic rollback triggers: if p99 > +5% or lease_escalations > 10/min then rollback.
Emma Li: Action items: Maya add CI workload + fairness test; Jun prototype lease escalation + reconcile loop; Ryan add telemetry and dashboard; Emma write RFC for admission API + rollout plan. If +1 I'll spin up canary.
Jun Park: +1
Ryan Chen: +1
Maya Shah: +1
Emma Li: I'll draft RFC this afternoon and tag the group. thanks :rocket:
